## Advance several blocks in one process (`distribute.blocks_per_process`) {#sec-ch01-mesh}

### Summary

Mesh clones and repartitions block options, then runs local blocks through a worker pool. On CUDA the pool assigns a
stream to each worker and fences caller and worker work with events. Mesh advances before exchanging, including its
one-block fast path.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** N/A (a code map): a `Mesh` clones and repartitions the block options, then advances its local blocks through a worker pool; on CUDA each worker has a stream and the caller fences with events.

**Data.** No physical quantity of its own. In: one block options tree and `blocks_per_process` (a count). Out: the local blocks, each with its own variable map, advanced and exchanged (the one-block fast path included).

**Placement.** The mesh advances all local blocks, then exchanges.

**Activation.** YAML `distribute.blocks_per_process` (default 1); the worker pool is used for more than one local block.

**Guarantee / limits.** A map; no convergence order. A block waits at most 5 minutes for its $x_1$ anchor (@sec-ch03-x1seams).

**Evidence.** `test_mesh_multi_block.release` asserts the local and remote neighbour ghosts (`allclose` defaults); `test_mesh_exchange_python` asserts the selected neighbour slab (exact); no run of these ctest entries is recorded for this chapter at the pin (missing evidence).
:::

### Derivation

No separate derivation: this section describes an interface or control-flow path. Numerical operators are derived in
their owning chapters.

### Numerical method

For several local blocks the per-block gravity fixer is deferred. On the final stage Mesh sums local budgets, performs
one process-group SUM, applies the common correction, refills physical boundaries and exchanges ghosts. Time-step
selection takes a local minimum followed by one group minimum. Redo combines local flags before one reduction. Stream
assignment is an execution policy, not evidence of numerical equivalence between decompositions.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
A driver-split source after a Mesh call can make previously exchanged ghosts stale before the next advance. This is an
inference from call order, not a measured drift. Remote block message tags reject more than 16 blocks per process. The
local x1 anchor wait requires concurrent or top-down producers and fails after its five-minute timeout.
:::
